source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Log into the BMC WebUI and navigate to SMTP setting page.
2. Under SMTP server options, enter in the IP address of your SMTP server. (If your SMTP server requires authentication, check the box next to requires authentication, and enter in the username and password.)
3. Select the authentication method.
4. Ensure you can connect to the SMTP server.
5. Configure the server for email alerts and cause an alert (power off/power on should be easy to cause).

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. SMTP server should receive the same event information from BMC.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "SMTP|IP Address"; echo ---sel-last---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel list last 3 2>&1; echo ---mail---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel get 0x0010 2>&1 | head -5
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return BMC `lan print` SMTP/IP lines plus the latest SEL entries, so the user can confirm the SMTP server config and see whether a generated event gets delivered to the SMTP server (operator checks the mail server inbox).
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: requires an SMTP server IP/credential to be configured and a reachable mail server to receive the event; event-delivery verification is confirmed at the mail server, operator-side.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly notes that mailbox receipt is operator-side, but its command only reads BMC state, assumes SMTP appears under `lan print`, uses a fixed SEL record `0x0010`, exposes credentials and supplies no SMTP-server or message evidence; it cannot prove delivery or content equality.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires isolated SMTP, protected authentication, approved event and server-side correlation. This review retains that classification and makes substitution versus power-event coverage explicit.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 829/2291 repeats the BMC-only command without validating the fixed record ID, server receipt, TLS/authentication, recipient safety or event-to-message mapping.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-993 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently retains package classification and adds exact transport phases, message-field comparison and event coverage accounting.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves functional alert delivery and forbids a read-only SEL substitute; ED-36 treats SMTP/event details as readiness inputs; ED-38 prohibits unapproved power control, automatic retry and AI-owned DUT verdict.

original_test_intent: Configure the BMC SMTP client and alert recipient, prove the approved transport/authentication connects, trigger a defined BMC event, and verify the SMTP server/mailbox receives a message containing the same event information.
original_method: An operator configures the BMC WebUI with the approved SMTP service, authentication and recipient, then causes the approved alert event. BMC event/SEL evidence, SMTP transaction logs and the delivered message are timestamped and compared field by field. Power off/on is the source's example stimulus but is never authorized by this review alone.
manual_activity: A qualified operator approves/configures WebUI SMTP, protects credentials, authorizes the exact event and any power transition, confirms mailbox authority and restores configuration. Automation can validate TLS/SMTP transactions, collect BMC/SEL/server/message evidence and compare event fields.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC/firmware/network identity and supported SMTP server fields, port, DNS/IP, TLS mode, certificate/hostname validation and authentication mechanisms
Controlled lab SMTP server, scoped account, sender envelope/header identity, test-only recipient/mailbox, relay policy, filtering and retention

One approved reversible event with exact sensor/source/type/assertion/severity/timestamp/sequence and unique correlation token where supported; explicit decision whether power off/on is required or merely the source example
Expected mapping from BMC event/SEL to SMTP envelope, subject, body, severity, source, timestamp/timezone and any vendor event identifier
Connection and delivery timeouts, maximum messages, retry/duplicate policy, prior BMC SMTP state, protected secret injection, maintenance window and cleanup/restore plan
safety_requirements: Use only an isolated test SMTP service and recipient. Do not send to production distribution lists, external recipients or an unrestricted relay.
Never expose BMC or SMTP credentials in command arguments, screenshots or logs; use protected entry/storage and verify TLS identity rather than disabling certificate checks.
Do not execute power off/on, reset or any event injection without separate engineer approval on a dedicated SUT. The source example is not authorization.

If Project SPEC chooses a lower-risk vendor test alert, record it as an override with original power example, actual event, approval and coverage difference; do not claim power-event notification was verified unless it was executed.
Do not use a fixed SEL ID such as `0x0010`; baseline the log and correlate the newly generated event by identity and timestamps. Preserve existing records rather than clearing unrelated logs.
Limit the run to the approved event and message count. Do not automatically retry on timeout because BMC/SMTP retry queues may later deliver duplicates and obscure the first failure.

Stop on wrong recipient, wrong event, unexpected mail volume, credential leak, TLS/authentication failure, host impact or uncertain correlation. Restore BMC SMTP settings, revoke/rotate exposed secrets and preserve the first-failure evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate SMTP/TLS/authentication, recipient and event-to-message contracts without configuring DUT or triggering events.
After operator approval and setup, capture the new BMC event, SMTP connection/TLS/auth/queue/receipt logs and raw redacted message, then compare approved fields deterministically.
Distinguish configuration success, server acceptance and final mailbox delivery; none alone proves all stages.
Do not enter secrets, trigger power/event changes without approval, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the SMTP security/recipient package, exact event, power requirement or override, field mapping, timeouts and cleanup.
Configure/observe the BMC WebUI and controlled mailbox, authorize the one event and intervene on delivery or host impact.
Restore SMTP/recipient/event state, review correlation and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Recent SEL output can support event correlation, but the literal sequence is insufficient and unsafe: SMTP may not be represented by `lan print`, the fixed record may be unrelated, `-P` exposes the password, and no SMTP transaction or delivered message is collected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported SMTP configuration/connection path with protected credentials, one approved uniquely identifiable event, and controlled server/mailbox APIs or logs. Compare the new event to the received message; exact tools depend on the Project SMTP service.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC WebUI SMTP server/authentication, connectivity, email-alert setup, source power-cycle example, same-event-information Criteria, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot config/logs; configure trusted test SMTP and recipient; verify transport without leaking secrets; trigger one approved event; correlate BMC/SEL, SMTP acceptance and mailbox delivery; compare event fields; observe retry/duplicates without retriggering; restore and clean up.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC SMTP implementation, controlled mail service and approved event source.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/WebUI, TLS library, SMTP server, authentication and mailbox client/API versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC SMTP alert specification, Project mail security policy and approved event-generation plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure transport identity, deterministic new-event correlation, server-side receipt, field mapping, retry limits and cleanup while retaining the source alert workflow.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: BMC configuration or SEL-only evidence does not prove delivery; SMTP server acceptance may not prove mailbox delivery; a synthetic test event does not automatically cover the source's power event.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: SMTP/security/recipient, event/map, timeouts/retry, approval, recovery and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Misconfiguration can disclose management events or credentials, create mail storms or affect host power when the example stimulus is used.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select a vendor-approved test alert instead of the source's power off/on example if it exercises the same SMTP pipeline, but must document the original and actual stimuli, engineer approval, equivalence and whether power-event content remains unverified.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/network identity, prior SMTP state and approved server/port/TLS/certificate/auth/sender/recipient package
Redacted WebUI configuration and transport connection/TLS/authentication result without secrets
Approved stimulus authorization and timestamp plus uniquely identified new BMC/SEL event with expected field map
SMTP server connection/queue/acceptance log and delivered raw/redacted test message with envelope, headers, subject/body and receipt timestamp
Field-by-field event/message comparison, observed delivery latency and duplicate/retry status
Restored BMC SMTP settings, cleaned test recipient/credentials as authorized, no residual queue/mail storm, retained logs and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently target end-to-end SMTP event delivery. The event and mail-field specifics are Project readiness inputs, and power off/on is phrased as an example rather than a mandatory contradictory method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The notification purpose and delivery criterion are clear. SMTP service, recipient, event, mapping and recovery are supplyable execution inputs; lack of them during review does not permanently block the case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains useful SEL support but rejects BMC-only evidence, fixed ID and secret handling as proof of delivery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and adds explicit coverage accounting if a non-power event is selected.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists reasoning with end-to-end transport and message correlation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently retains package classification and strengthens first-failure, retry and event-substitution boundaries.

review_improvement: Prevents an unrelated SEL record or configured-but-undelivered SMTP path from passing, while avoiding unauthorized power control and production-mail exposure.
independent_technical_reasoning: SMTP alert acceptance is end-to-end and causal: the newly generated BMC event must be the reason a specific message arrived. That requires evidence from both endpoints and a unique time/field correlation. Because setup and event authorization are human-controlled but delivery analysis is strongly automatable, package/user confirmation is the correct boundary.
